dimensions.finding: The retention LegalRule links the Article 1 definition of record, preserving notice plus receipt timestamp as its source context. Articles 1-4 were not invented as separate operative duties.

The LegalRule retains receipt-based timing and preserving the notice text and its limiting language. Its only EngineeringRule criterion states retention for 7 days; it omits when the period begins, notice-and-timestamp storage, and preservation of limiting language. Its evidence list only requests retention-policy configuration, with supporting log retention. This cannot fully assess the software obligations declared covered.

The retention LegalRule states the temporary-test-record exception, but the EngineeringRule criterion and applicability guidance omit it. REL-6 also labels Article 3 as an EXCEPTION on the in-person duty, although the source explicitly says that exception does not remove Article 6. The source relationship is represented with the wrong semantic kind.

The retention rule retains source links for definition, scope, exception, cross-reference and receipt-timing context in Articles 1-4. Their hashes resolve to the pinned synthetic corpus. This does not cure the EngineeringRule omissions or the erroneous exception relation.

The Article 6 rule keeps appointment of a person, annual session, in-person attendance and organizer register context. It is NON_ASSESSABLE with nonRepositoryDuty true and has no invented repository criterion.
Authored rule references resolve to the current immutable synthetic corpus chunk IDs. Every source and context reference matches its exact accepted document locator and content hash.
